sources.description:
Khalil Fong’s Final Portrait

This studio portrait of Khalil Fong features the singer-songwriter in a blue sweatshirt and round glasses, set against a plain white background. His composed expression and casual attire echo the understated elegance he brought to his music and public appearances.

Fong passed away on February 21, 2025, at age 41 after a five-year battle with illness, as confirmed by his label Fu Music. Celebrated for his fusion of R&B, soul, and Mandarin pop, he left behind a legacy of heartfelt songs and cross-cultural influence. Fans in Japan and around the world continue to honor his gentle spirit and timeless voice.

sources.description:
Portrait of Khalil Fong

Khalil Fong appears in a studio portrait wearing a white double-breasted suit jacket over a black turtleneck, his dark hair tousled and round glasses perched on his nose. The neutral gray background and his composed posture highlight his refined style and thoughtful gaze.

A pioneering figure in Mandarin R&B and soul, Fong debuted in 2005 with SoulBoy and rose to fame with albums like Ai Ai Ai and Future. He founded FU Music in 2016, produced films and children’s books, and won the Golden Melody Award for Best Mandarin Male Singer. His final album, The Dreamer, was released in 2024 before his passing in 2025.

sources.description:
Khalil Fong Portrait

Khalil Fong sits casually on a clear acrylic chair, turned around so that the chair’s backrest supports his arms. He wears a beige cardigan over a white shirt, accented by a dark bow tie and round glasses, projecting a blend of sophistication and ease. His black pants and blue-detail sneakers add a modern, relaxed touch against the minimalist studio background.

This photograph appears as the first image in a three-picture gallery on 360百科, under the title “方大同.” The gallery’s layout and the neutral setting focus attention on Fong’s distinctive style and composed expression.
